title: Williams College (Williams)
summary: Williams College (Williams) is a university in Williamstown. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Williams.

sections.heading: What Williams is known for
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) is a private nonprofit institution known for its selective undergraduate education. With an enrollment of approximately 2,076 students, Williams maintains a highly competitive admission rate of 8.25%, reflecting its status as a prestigious liberal arts college. The college does not offer programs in health or business fields, focusing instead on a broad range of other academic disciplines. As a private nonprofit entity, Williams emphasizes a commitment to providing a rigorous and comprehensive educational experience.

sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) maintains a highly selective undergraduate admissions process, with an admission rate of approximately 8.25%. The college seeks to enroll students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and potential. The average SAT score for admitted students is 1533, reflecting the institution's rigorous academic standards. Williams evaluates applicants holistically, considering various aspects of their academic and personal backgrounds. The college's admissions policies emphasize a comprehensive review to identify candidates who will thrive in its challenging educational environment.

sections.heading: How to read Williams tuition
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) charges a tuition fee of $68,560 for both in-state and out-of-state students. This uniform tuition rate applies regardless of residency status. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as room, board, and fees, amounts to $84,860. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families anticipate the financial commitment required for enrollment at Williams.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) offers financial aid to support students from diverse economic backgrounds. Approximately 17.61% of its student body receives Pell Grants, indicating a commitment to assisting lower-income students. Among those who complete their studies, the median debt stands at $12,761, reflecting the college's efforts to minimize student borrowing. Prospective students can explore personalized cost estimates and financial aid options through Williams' official net price calculator, available on their website, as well as through the College Scorecard platform.

sections.heading: Colleges and schools
paragraphs: Williams College does not have separate colleges or schools within its academic structure. Instead, it operates as a single, unified institution offering a broad range of programs across the liberal arts and sciences. This structure allows for an interdisciplinary approach to education, encouraging students to explore diverse fields of study within one cohesive academic environment.

sections.heading: Academic features
paragraphs: Williams College offers a rigorous academic environment characterized by a low student-faculty ratio of 6 to 1, fostering close interaction between students and professors. This intimate setting supports personalized instruction and mentorship across its diverse liberal arts curriculum. The college emphasizes interdisciplinary study, enabling students to engage deeply with multiple fields while benefiting from the expertise of a dedicated faculty. Williams' academic features are designed to promote critical thinking, collaborative learning, and comprehensive intellectual development within a supportive community.

sections.heading: Degree levels
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) offers undergraduate degree programs exclusively, focusing on a liberal arts education. The institution does not provide graduate or professional degrees, maintaining its commitment to a comprehensive undergraduate experience. This approach aligns with Williams' emphasis on small class sizes and close faculty-student interaction, fostering a rigorous academic environment tailored to bachelor's level studies.

sections.heading: Housing and dining

Information about off-campus housing costs is not specified, indicating that the primary housing arrangements are centered on campus. sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for Williams College (Williams) graduates demonstrate strong post-graduation success. The college has a high completion rate, with approximately 93.61% of students finishing their degrees within 150% of the expected time. Median earnings for alumni tend to increase over time, with graduates earning a median income of $71,754 six years after enrollment and $88,665 ten years after enrollment. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is $12,761, reflecting the financial investment associated with attending Williams. These figures indicate that Williams graduates generally achieve favorable economic outcomes following their education.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) demonstrates a balanced gender distribution, with women comprising approximately 52.46% of the student body and men making up about 47.54%. The college's racial and ethnic composition includes 46.63% White students, 14.11% Hispanic students, 12.48% Asian students, and 6.07% Black students. This diversity reflects Williams' commitment to fostering an inclusive campus environment. Additionally, about 17.61% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a presence of students from lower-income backgrounds. These figures highlight Williams' efforts to maintain a diverse and supportive academic community.

sections.heading: Is Williams accredited?
paragraphs: Williams College (Williams) is a private liberal arts college located in Williamstown, Massachusetts. It is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), which is a regional accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Accreditation by NECHE ensures that Williams meets established standards of quality and effectiveness in its educational programs and institutional operations.
